messages:
Ash Patel: Quick follow-up from the continuous-batching RFC — want to sync on admission/eviction interface boundaries and a couple of corner cases I ran into while prototyping.
Marco Li: SG. What did you run into? :eyes:
Ash Patel: Two things: (1) partial-eviction API: how much of a batch can caller evict vs runtime deciding, and (2) streaming/interactive requests that hold KV cache long enough to block packing heuristics.
Sophie Nguyen: For (1) I'd prefer the runtime expose a soft API: callers can mark a subset of requests as "evictable" and the runtime can pick oldest-from-evictable when under pressure. Keeps back-and-forth out of hot path.
Devon R.: That sounds good, but we need an explicit signal for urgency. Some customers will set deadline hints; we should not implicitly assume evictable == low priority.
Ash Patel: Agreed. Proposal: request envelope carries {deadline_hint, evictable_flag, priority_tier}. Eviction policy is: respect deadlines first, then priority_tier, then evictable_flag age. If none, runtime will preempt lowest token-affinity batches.
Marco Li: How do we expose preemption to callers? We don't want callers to have to implement complex retries.
Sophie Nguyen: Provide a simple status callback in the sync API and a streaming control frame in the streaming API. Eg: on_preempt(reason) with codes {capacity, deadline_conflict, kv_pressure}. Client lib can auto-retry or fallback to smaller model.
Ash Patel: Example control frame for streaming:
```
> CONTROL: preempt kv_pressure
tokens_consumed: 42
suggested_fallback: gpt-small-8k
```
Devon R.: About (2) KV cache pinning — interactive requests can keep KV in GPU longer than their generation latency, breaking packing assumptions. Two options: (A) treat KV pin as a separate scarce resource with quota per tenant, or (B) opportunistically spill KV to CPU/NVMe for low-priority requests.
Marco Li: (A) is simpler to reason about for fairness. We could surface "kv_budget" in tenant config (e.g., 100MB active KV). If over-budget, runtime throttles new interactive sessions or converts them to CPU-backed execution.
Sophie Nguyen: But (B) gives better latency degradation curve for noisy-but-latent workloads: spill cold segments to NVMe and keep hot prefixes on GPU. Implementation complexity is higher.
Ash Patel: I'm leaning (A) + controlled spill as a follow-up. First cut: kv_budget + eviction whitelist for special SLA tenants (allow override).
Devon R.: Observability needs: we must emit per-queue "eviction_attempts", "preempt_reasons", "kv_pinned_bytes", and per-tenant headroom gauge. These enable autoscaler rules and SLO alerts.
Marco Li: Also add a latency histogram split by admission_reason (immediate, packed, after_preempt). Helps detect pathological preemption loops.
Sophie Nguyen: API surface note: avoid exposing queue internals to customers — keep signals high-level. Internals: lane IDs, slice offsets are runtime-only.
Ash Patel: Implementation plan (short):
- Add request envelope fields (deadline_hint, evictable_flag, priority_tier, kv_budget_hint)
- Admission layer reads kv_budget and current_pinned_bytes; reject or downgrade if over.
- Eviction controller: maintains evictable deque per tenant, supports partial batch eviction up to N requests with an "atomic splice".
- Control frames for streaming preempt events + small SDK change
- Metrics: eviction_attempts, preempt_reasons, kv_pinned_bytes, headroom_gauge, admission_latency_by_reason
Marco Li: Sounds actionable. One nit: "atomic splice" for partial eviction — need to keep KV indices consistent. If we remove items from middle of batch, we must rewrite batch offsets or copy KV pointers.
Sophie Nguyen: Suggestion: avoid mid-batch holes by allowing only prefix/suffix evictions on a given batch. That keeps offset math trivial and minimizes memory moves.
Ash Patel: Yeah, prefix-only eviction per batch simplifies very much. If we need in-middle later, we can implement a compaction pass.
Devon R.: Backpressure protocol: when admission rejects due to kv_budget, return structured error with suggested wait or suggested_fallback (e.g., CPU path). Do not rely on HTTP 503 alone.
Marco Li: Agree. Also add a reclaim hint header from runtime: "X-Reclaim-ETA" so SDK can schedule reattempts without busy polls.
Sophie Nguyen: For testing, we should build a microbench harness that simulates interactive sessions with pinned KV and verify packing efficiency and SLO under different kv_budget values.
Ash Patel: I'll draft a follow-up RFC patch with the API fields, control frame examples, and the prefix-eviction guarantee. Will add microbench results from my prototype.
runtime-bot: Deploy preview for branch continuous-batcher/kv-budget landed on staging (build 4257). :package:
Devon R.: Nice. Can we merge the metrics schema PR before the RFC so dashboards exist when we run experiments?
Ash Patel: Yes — I'll fast-track metrics PR today and link it in the RFC.
Marco Li: Thanks team. If nobody objects, I'll implement the admission kv_budget check next sprint and pair with Ash on the eviction deque logic.
Sophie Nguyen: No objections. One doc ask: add an explicit section in the RFC that calls out "no mid-batch hole guarantees" so we don't accidentally promise it to customers.
Ash Patel: Done. I'll add that and ping infra for the NVMe spill spike later.
Devon R.: :thumbsup: End-to-end looks solid.
